skill.displayName: 企业所得税纳税调整核对（免费版）

llm.summary: This appears to be a local tax-table checking skill, but its claims about what it verifies are inconsistent enough that users should review it before relying on it.

dimensions.detail: Read and Bash access are proportionate for a local checker that reads an input file and runs bundled JavaScript; inspection found no broad local indexing or credential/session access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, package manager steps, remote payload retrieval, or external dependencies were found; the skill ships local Markdown, JavaScript, and sample JSON files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are mostly scoped to running a local Node script on a user-provided tax adjustment table, but there are inconsistencies around anonymous usage statistics and the exact checks performed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, file writes, privilege escalation, background worker, destructive operation, or implemented network call was found in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent, but the artifact overstates assurance in a tax-compliance workflow: it advertises per-item checking and source-backed conclusions while the engine implements a narrower set of arithmetic/table consistency checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this only as a limited local arithmetic consistency helper for the listed free checks. Do not treat a clean result as tax-compliance clearance, especially for withheld limit-based checks such as entertainment, advertising, donation caps, taxable loss, or tax-rate applicability. I found no implemented network call or persistence, but the documentation should be reviewed because some scope and usage-statements are inconsistent.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced runner script is present and was inspected locally; the partial-coverage concern did not hold after inspection.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese user-facing text is expected for a Chinese enterprise income tax adjustment checker; this is a localization/usability issue rather than evidence of unsafe behavior.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The concern is supported: the implementation reports line-oriented arithmetic findings, but does not provide the stronger source-cited conclusion coverage implied by the metadata.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The concern is partly supported: the free version lists withheld limit checks, but other wording and the runtime disclaimer can still imply those limit-based tax checks are covered.
[SDI-4] expected: The low-severity comment about a contract example is minor documentation drift and does not materially change the security posture.
